instructions: Cut the 1.25 lb chicken thighs into 3/4-inch pieces.

Shake the can of coconut milk well. In a bowl, mix 1/4 cup of the coconut milk with 1 tbsp curry powder, 1 tsp of the sugar, 2 tsp of the curry paste and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Add the chicken, toss until it's coated and leave it for 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the peanut sauce. In a small saucepan, stir together the rest of the coconut milk, the remaining 2 tbsp curry paste, 3/4 cup peanut butter, 1/4 cup sugar, 2 tsp dark soy sauce, the other 1/2 tsp salt, 2 tbsp vinegar and 3/4 cup water.

Set it over medium-low and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's smooth and thick but still pourable. If it's too thick, stir in a splash of water. Cover it and keep it warm on the lowest heat.
Thread 4 or 5 pieces of chicken onto each of the 16 skewers, pushing them close together.

Heat 1 1/2 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high. Lay in half the skewers and cook for 3 minutes, until the underside is golden with a few dark spots. Flip them and cook the other side for 3 minutes. You're cooking them to 175°F, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest piece. No thermometer? Cut into one: it's done when there's no pink left in the middle.
Move them to a platter. Add the other 1 1/2 tbsp oil and cook the second batch the same way.
Meanwhile, finely chop the 2 tbsp peanuts and pick a small handful of cilantro leaves. Thinly slice the red chili into a little dish for the table and cut the lime into wedges.
Taste the peanut sauce, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Pour the sauce into a bowl and scatter half the peanuts on top. Scatter the rest of the peanuts and the cilantro over the skewers.
Serve the skewers with the peanut sauce, lime wedges and sliced chili on the side.
method_notes: Both marinate thigh pieces with curry flavors and sugar, thread them on skewers, cook them hot until charred at the edges and serve a sweet peanut sauce made with coconut milk and red curry paste. RecipeTin Eats, the lead, marinates in a little coconut milk with curry powder and curry paste for 20 minutes, pan fries the skewers 3 minutes a side and simmers the rest of the can with peanut butter, sugar, dark soy, vinegar and water. Once Upon a Chef marinates in soy, brown sugar, ketchup, turmeric and coriander for 4 hours or more, grills them, and sharpens its sauce with lime juice and sriracha. This one follows the lead in a skillet and keeps the chili on the side.
